title: What is the difference between strategy, operations, technology and implementation consulting?
description: The main types of consulting work explained simply, with examples of the questions each answers and which firms tend to do each.
hook: "Consulting" covers very different jobs. A strategy consultant might spend six weeks deciding whether a company should enter India; an implementation consultant might spend a year rolling out a new system across 40 countries. Knowing the difference helps you choose which firms and roles to apply for.
body:
Strategy consulting: what should we do?

Big direction-setting questions for senior leaders: which markets to enter, whether to buy a company, how to grow, how to respond to a competitor. Projects are often short and intense, and end with a recommendation. This is the work most associated with McKinsey, BCG and Bain, and with the strategy arms of larger firms.

Operations consulting: how do we do it better?

Making the business run faster, cheaper or more reliably: supply chains, procurement, manufacturing, customer service, hospital flow. More hands-on data and process work.

Technology and digital consulting

Choosing and implementing systems, cloud, data platforms, AI and cybersecurity, and redesigning how the business works around technology. Firms like Accenture and the Big Four have very large technology practices.

Implementation consulting: making it happen

Strategy work tends to end at the decision; implementation work continues until the change is delivered and the results show up. It is often longer, with bigger teams working alongside the client.

The lines blur

Most firms do some of everything. Strategy firms increasingly help with implementation, and large firms have dedicated strategy teams. In the Big Four, the strategy groups are where the work looks most like MBB. What matters for you is the practice, the role and the kind of problems you would work on, not just the firm's name.

Which suits you?

  • Enjoy big open questions and fast pace? Look at strategy roles.
  • Enjoy seeing changes through and working closely with operations? Look at operations or implementation roles.
  • Enjoy technology and building things? Look at technology consulting.
